allSourceAssessments.independentSupportingSummary: The complete undated guide maps four domains and 27 subskills; data management carries 25–30%. It supplies objective scope, not SDK correctness or proof that AI-200 is generally available.

The connection-best-practices section places pools and routing state in the application-lifetime CosmosClient; lightweight container handles differ from network operations. read_item accepts item and partition_key. The if_match illustration and sweeping key-privilege prose are not used.

The actual @name/value parameter examples separate data from SQL, partition_key addresses one partition, SELECT controls projection, and max_item_count controls pages. Iterator consumption executes requests. This does not establish universal plan caching, per-page RU totals or cross-query continuation guarantees.

The current policy table expressly includes float16 alongside float32/int8/uint8; path, dimensions and metric describe a container-created immutable policy. Flat is exhaustive with a 505-dimension bound; quantizedFlat compresses; diskANN approximates. The contradictory cosine-score direction is not adopted.

The retrieved unit contains VectorDistance, TOP, parameter binding and brute-force arguments, but contradicts its ascending examples with higher-score-is-better prose. No candidate cites this unit for score interpretation; its presence creates no documentation-parent permission.

WHERE predicates express eligible metadata and partition_key selects the tenant partition. The unit expressly discusses optimizer-dependent pre/post filtering. It does not promise every eligible nearest neighbor or a full TOP count; hybrid RRF claims are not needed.

Push processing uses leases for ownership and checkpoints; pull processing lets the application schedule reads and save continuation. Hashing only title/content and persisting the hash with its vector prevents unchanged-input refresh. Exactly-once wording and the malformed start_time example are excluded.

Composite ORDER BY requires the property sequence and supports reversal of every direction, not one direction alone. Additional indexes cost writes. New indexes require completed transformation and old users must drain before removing their support. Removal is not guaranteed to fall back successfully.

Flat compares original vectors, quantizedFlat compares compressed vectors, and diskANN uses approximate navigation. The dimension/population bounds and immutable policy constrain these choices. Optional build tuning cannot change dimensionality; no Preview tuning entitlement is assumed.

The actual response_hook example calls list(results) before inspecting response metadata. Unqueried content can be excluded without deleting its body; composite additions complete asynchronously. Fixed RU savings and last-response totals are not established.

Session state is client-managed and partition-bound; another instance requires the relevant token for read-your-writes. Tokenless independent sessions can lag. This does not strengthen account consistency or guarantee newly written vectors have reached an asynchronous index.

The connection unit uses token.token from the ossrdbms-aad scope, distinguishes CA/hostname verification, and gives direct 5432 versus enabled built-in pooler 6432 on GP/MO. Identity mapping and trusted roots remain prerequisites; no universal username format is adopted.

NOT NULL, foreign keys and compound uniqueness enforce different invariants. JSONB supports nested variable metadata while BYTEA and VARCHAR represent binary and character data. Incorrect default-RESTRICT and absolute trailing-index-column prose are not used.

The complete unit describes JSON extraction, keyset pagination, RETURNING and upserts. Its alias-scope table is not reliable for all PostgreSQL clauses and has no supporting role for this cohort. External T-SQL resources are not borrowed.

psycopg execute binds %s using a separate tuple, unlike Python formatting. Connection and cursor contexts have different cleanup scopes, and pools lend connections. Syntax/constraint failures require correction; a confirmed transient connection reset can justify bounded recovery.

vector(n) constrains dimensions and supports typed dense vectors; additional vector columns provide different document representations. The operator table distinguishes cosine <=>, L2 <-> and negative inner product <#>. Extension installation/allowlisting is not silently supplied by a query.

HNSW has no representative-data training dependency; IVFFlat clusters existing data. vector_cosine_ops pairs with <=>, not <->. EXPLAIN can diagnose eligibility. The actual unit directly links the performance article; no universal ANN latency/recall figures are adopted.

Index statistics report accumulated use, size functions measure current structures, and MVCC keeps old row versions until reusable. An embedding_stale marker separates edit persistence from later batch regeneration. The broken 3072-dimensional ordinary-vector HNSW sample is not used.

A small metadata-selected candidate set can legitimately use distance sorting instead of HNSW. Distance acceptance and LIMIT count solve different problems; source fields can accompany chunks. Actual plan evidence is necessary; WHERE does not universally force physical prefiltering.

Source documents plus ordered chunk rows support adjacency and source lookup. The reference supplies citation fields, quality thresholds, neighbor expansion and chunk-token tradeoffs. These are independent retrieval obligations, not guarantees of generated-answer truth.

shared_buffers caches pages, effective_cache_size is a nonallocating planner estimate, and work_mem applies to individual operations under concurrency. Query effort controls differ from memory. The quadratic-dimensional-compute assertion is false and the simplified hash budget is insufficient for a hard upper bound.

The full index unit distinguishes lists/probes from HNSW graph construction/search effort and discusses concurrent builds. Its fixed-size, fixed-speed and automatic-quality generalizations are not necessary for these questions and receive no approval.

Typed frequent metadata can use supporting indexes; selective predicates can reduce candidate work, and EXPLAIN establishes the actual plan. Vector element storage is linear in dimensions. Its broad index/JSON performance generalizations do not override workload measurements.

Read replicas are read-only and asynchronously updated, so immediate confirmations remain on the primary. Actual memory/CPU/IO and index working sets guide scaling. Scenario throughput is measured input, not a product limit; illustrative tier tables and price claims are unused.

Built-in PgBouncer uses 6432 on GP/MO; transaction pooling retains one backend only during a transaction. SET LOCAL scopes query tuning, and pool.connection returns a borrowed connection even on exceptions. Startup SET is not a per-transaction guarantee; blanket reset claims are excluded.

OSS multi-key commands require same-slot keys; Enterprise supports cross-slot MGET. SCAN is preferred to blocking KEYS, and pipelining reduces command overhead without creating a one-command interface. No arbitrary Redis.io or GitHub link becomes an AI-200 source.

The actual command examples distinguish SET/GET strings, HASH fields, numeric-string INCRBY and Lists. EXPIRE adds a key lifetime, PERSIST removes it, SETEX also writes a string, and deleting an updated cache entry supports cache-aside. This is not cross-database atomicity.

IndexDefinition prefix controls monitored key membership; HASH vectors use packed bytes with matching TYPE/DIM. KNN, VECTOR_RANGE and per-request EF_RUNTIME serve different contracts. The claim that all pipelines are atomic and the unindexed category example are not relied on.

FLOAT32 and FLOAT64 occupy four/eight bytes per component; TYPE/DIM must match. HNSW EF_RUNTIME changes exploration whereas FLAT changes algorithm. Precision reduction needs evaluation; no guaranteed recall, speed or blanket text-versus-image metric rule is adopted.

HASH represents flat fields with packed-vector bytes; JSON represents nested documents and numeric arrays, with JSONPath-indexed fields. This is a representation contract, not guaranteed memory/speed superiority, and the same-key HASH-to-JSON migration sample is not adopted.

The directly training-linked product article establishes dimensioned index columns, the ordinary-vector 2000-dimension index bound, all-lists IVFFlat exact-plan behavior, operator/class matching and measured EXPLAIN. Its HNSW transaction example omits LOCAL despite the prose; the valid IVFFlat LOCAL example supplies the scoped-setting claim.
